_note: v4 investigation sequences. 'built': true when the sequence exists in the game; Danny only hints about built ones. Hints are plain spoken English.

puzzles.name: Walk the Room
hints: Before anything gets moved, Chief, check every way in or out of that office: the door bolt, the window, the stove pipe, the ceiling, the floor vent and the floor itself. Mark each one possible or impossible.

Try the bolt with a bit of thread, look at the window bars and the stove pipe, and knock on the floor. Only one of those six could let a person through. Use your camera plates on the things that matter: the body, the decanter, the bolt, the note and the music box.
The door bolt, the window, the stove pipe, the ceiling and the vent are all impossible. The floor is the only one you should mark possible.

puzzles.name: The Body
puzzles.mechanic: Guided examination with an unreliable narrator
hints: Doctor Lindqvist will talk you through the body, Chief, but watch what he skips. Look at everything yourself.
Heart failure doesn't turn skin pink or leave a smell on the breath. Check the skin, the settled blood and the mouth.
The three things that don't fit a heart attack: the cherry-pink settled blood, the faint bitter-almond smell at the mouth, and the pink colour of his skin and nails.

puzzles.name: Time of Death
puzzles.mechanic: Cooling calculation with a sliding window
hints: Bodies cool at roughly one and a half degrees an hour, Chief. Work backwards from the thermometer reading.
Normal is 98.6. Take away the reading, divide by 1.5, and count back from the time you took it. Then check the stiffness and the settled blood agree.
He was 84.6 at seven o'clock: that's fourteen degrees, about nine hours and twenty minutes of cooling. So around twenty to ten last night. Set a window like quarter past nine to ten.

puzzles.name: The Bench Test
puzzles.mechanic: Six drops, four samples, three reagents
hints: Six drops of test chemical, five samples, Chief. Don't waste drops before you know what each chemical shows.
You need the chart that says which chemical reacts to what. Ask the doctor nicely, use my reference book, or force the kit open.
Put chemical B on the decanter brandy and on the glass: deep blue means cyanide. The heart drops go brown with C, but that's only his medicine.

puzzles.name: The Safe
hints: Pryce loved riddles. The combination is three numbers, and the answers are on the office walls and in his pocket.

'Her years' is the age written under the girl in the photograph, 'the wings' hearts' is the number of engines on the plane in the picture, and 'the minute the sky stopped' is on his stopped pocket watch.
Nineteen, three, seventeen: left to nineteen, right to three, left to seventeen.

puzzles.name: The Floor, the Box and the Latch
puzzles.mechanic: Knock and listen, then play back the tune
hints: Knock on the floor, Chief, and listen. Then listen to that music box all the way through.
The hollow spot is under the rug. The music box has numbered teeth, and the bookshelf has eight pull-books. Each note of the tune is a book.
Pull the books in this order: five, three, one, three, five, eight, five, three.

puzzles.name: Readied for Flight
hints: The Trimotor in the hangar was being got ready for a flight, Chief. Climb into the cabin and look around.
Look at everything: the cot, the straps, the trunk, the hat box, and the flight plan in the cockpit.
A stretcher with straps, a woman's trunk for 'E. Marsh', and a plan for Zürich at five. It was readied for a passenger lying down, sedated.

puzzles.name: The Chemical Shelf
hints: The darkroom storeroom in Operations has a stock ledger, Chief. Weigh the jars and see what's missing.
Two jars are light. Check the darkroom log: one of them has a good reason.
The cyanide is thirty grams short with nothing in the log. The silver nitrate was used for plates.

puzzles.name: The Darkroom
hints: Billie's old plates from the 1931 search are in the darkroom. Develop them carefully: you only get one retry each.
Expose when the needle is in the green band, and pull the plate out of the developer at about sixty seconds. Then compare plate four with the official photo.
On plate four: the truck tracks, the drag trail, and the bundle under the canvas aren't in the official photo.

puzzles.name: The Manifests and the Payout
hints: The records room in Operations has the Marigold's passenger cards, Chief. Count the dead.
Put the six cards in seat order, then match each to a death certificate. One won't have one.
Seat four, C. Pryce, nineteen: paid for, never certified dead.

puzzles.name: Raking Light
puzzles.mechanic: Read charred paper with a lamp
hints: The lounge fireplace in Operations is still warm, Chief. Somebody burned papers before dawn.
Move the lamp slowly around each sheet. Each line only shows at its own angle.
The letter is Vivienne leaving him, not killing him. The contract page has a forged signature: a pen line traced over pencil.

puzzles.name: The Blackout
hints: The hangar lights went out at noon, Chief. The fuse panel's in the maintenance shed.
The hangar, the radio and the beacon must be on. Don't overload either generator.
Hangar and beacon on generator 1, radio and the Quarters on generator 2. Then look under the panel.

puzzles.name: The Cracked Mount
hints: Ox's old engine mounts are on his bench in the maintenance shed. Test them for cracks.
Dye, wait, wipe, developer: in that order. Straight parallel lines are machining marks.
Mount 2, the Marigold's: the jagged branching line is a real crack.

puzzles.name: The Ration Stores
hints: Compare the ration ledger in the storage shed with the mess roster, Chief. Day by day.
Take the people fed away from the rations signed out. Then turn back through the ledger pages to see when it started.
It's one extra ration every day, signed by Ox, starting 16 November 1931.

puzzles.name: The Marks in the Dust
hints: Those scuffs in the dust are where the crates usually sit, Chief. Somebody moves them every day.
Push the crates back onto the curved marks. You can only push, never pull, so don't trap one against a wall.
Push the two top crates into the top corners, and walk the bottom-left one around to the bottom-right corner.

puzzles.name: The Night Burn
hints: Read every fuel gauge yourself, Chief, before you believe the ledger.
Compare today's reading with yesterday's, then check what Ox logged as issued.
Tank C, the Trimotor's, is 38 gallons short with nothing logged.

puzzles.name: The Smoke Test
hints: If there's a tunnel under the field, smoke will find it. There's a rusty vent pipe in the fuel farm yard, and smoke pots in the maintenance shed.

Take a smoke pot from the crate by the flare pots in the maintenance shed, light it in the vent pipe at the fuel farm, then go look in the hangar office, the storage shed and the darkroom. You have about forty minutes.
The smoke comes up through the office floor vent, the storage shed floor and the darkroom storeroom. Visit all three while it lasts.

puzzles.name: Follow the Wire
hints: Hobbs says someone has been tapping on the telegraph line. Listen to the telegram tape at his radio, Chief.
Compare the tape with each operator's sending: the speed, how even it is, and the stumble on the Q. Then follow the iron posts across the runway.
It's the unknown sender. The posts lead to a splice box by the maintenance shed, and the wire goes under the hangar wall.

puzzles.name: The Barograph Overlay
hints: Hobbs kept his original barograph traces. Lay the 1931 one over the official report.
Slide the tracing until the time marks line up, then look at the letter 'e' in the report under the magnifier.
Line it up at about 37. The chipped 'e' is Miss Quill's typewriter.

puzzles.name: The Last Call
hints: Hobbs kept a recording of the Marigold's last call. Listen to it all the way to the end.
The interesting part is near the end, after the engine screams. Scrub to about two minutes forty.
Mark it at around 2:40 to 2:48. It's a young woman calling 'Daddy'.

puzzles.name: The Stakeout
hints: The beacon keeper's log mentions a glow from the hangar roof at dusk. Go up the tower at half past four.
Wait for dusk, then sweep the binoculars along the hangar roof slowly.
The glow is at the roof vent, a little right of centre. Stop on it and say 'There!'.

puzzles.name: The Locked Case
hints: Doctor Lindqvist's leather case is on the office floor, next to his bag. He'll open it if he trusts you; otherwise I can get a warrant.
If you pick it: light tension only, and try each pin until one clicks. Heavy tension breaks picks.
The pins set in the order three, one, four, two, with light tension.

puzzles.name: The Prints
hints: Dust the things from the office and compare them with everyone's prints, Chief. Pattern, width and scars all have to match.
Use the callipers to measure each print. A loop is a little U shape, a whorl goes round in circles, an arch is a hump.
His glass is his own print. The decanter and the music box carry a small scarred loop, thirteen millimetres: that matches nobody at the dinner. Billie's is scarred but sixteen.

puzzles.name: Tamsin's Shorthand
hints: I fished Tamsin's ledger pages out of the kitchen stove, Chief. They're on my desk. It's a cipher: every letter stands for another.
It's a keyword alphabet. The keyword is a name everyone keeps saying.
The keyword is MARIGOLD.

puzzles.name: The Timeline
hints: Put the night in order, Chief. Start from the fixed points: the bolt at 21:25, the tune at ten, the door at 06:10.
Every card needs something you've actually found. Talk to Billie about the bang, Julian about where he was, and solve the time of death.
Dinner, the bolt, his death, the tune, the bang, Julian at the door, the note, the door broken down. In that order.
